lesson.title: Chardi Kala: Staying Hopeful and Joyful
lesson.subject: sikhi

contentBlocks.text: Sometimes things don't go the way we want — a game doesn't work out, or we feel disappointed. In Sikhi, choosing to stay hopeful, joyful, and kind even during hard moments is called Chardi Kala.

Chardi Kala doesn't mean pretending everything is perfect. It means choosing hope and courage even when things are hard. Think of a time something didn't go your way — maybe you lost a game or felt left out. What's one way you could respond with Chardi Kala instead of giving up or getting upset? Practice saying: 'Even though this is hard, I can stay hopeful.'
Chardi Kala is a strength you can practice, just like any other skill. This week, notice one moment when you choose hope over giving up.

objectives: Explain in simple words what Chardi Kala means (choosing hope and courage even during hard moments)
Identify one real example of practicing Chardi Kala in their own life
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Ask the child about a recent time something didn't go their way.
2. Introduce Chardi Kala as choosing hope and courage even when things are hard — not pretending everything is fine, but staying hopeful anyway.
3. Brainstorm together how they could respond to their earlier example with Chardi Kala.
4. Practice saying the phrase together: 'Even though this is hard, I can stay hopeful.'
5. Move to the worksheet: trace the word and talk through its meaning again.
6. Close by picking one moment this week to practice Chardi Kala.
differentiationTips: Struggling: use a very concrete, low-stakes example (losing a game) rather than an emotionally heavy one
Ready for more: talk about a time they saw someone else practice Chardi Kala — a family member, friend, or story character
For a child processing something genuinely difficult, keep this gentle and supportive rather than treating it as a lesson to complete
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and discussion activity — there is no right/wrong answer beyond correct word tracing. Check that the child can describe Chardi Kala in their own words and name one real example.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Chardi Kala is a foundational, universally-taught Sikhi value — introducing it through the child's own real experience builds genuine understanding before it's revisited in deeper historical and doctrinal context in later grades.

generationData.instructions: Trace the words, say them out loud, then write them once more on your own.
